issue.title: M4-11 — The demo tape records `once` dispatching a maker, and the README's alt text says so
issue.body:
Part of **M4, `docs/v0-build-plan.md` §4 M4**. **Author:** the PM, as the decomposing role (`D18` rule 4; `D20`). Filed by the PM on 2026-10-01, after the owner ratified the M4 decomposition at revision 6c ([Ratification](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5932237390)), from revision 6d, which applies the reviewer's 6c note.

Every citation below is archived on #467, the M4 decomposition record:
- "Ruling 1" to "ruling 5" are the architect's rulings: [1](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5925019458) (Q1–Q10, Delta 1–Delta 7), [2](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5925251185) (AQ1–AQ3, P1–P7), [3](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5925725145) (AQ4–AQ7, P8–P11), [4](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5925967483) (its Q1–Q3) with [its addendum](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5926071377) on `judgeDirectory`, and [5](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5926264058) (AQ8). "Ruling 5 on #332" is on #332, and "#423's ruling 3" on #423.
- `O1`–`O21` and "Ratification" are the owner's rulings: [O1–O8](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5925048252), [O9–O12](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5925251352), [O13](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5925312832), [O14, O15](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5925474724), [O16, O17](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5925759689), [O18](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5926065486), [O19](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5926433766), [O20, O21](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5926800423) and [Ratification](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5932237390).
- "reviewer N", "engineer N" and "Codex N" are the round-1 reviews ([reviewer](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5925460164), [engineer](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5925460338), [Codex](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5925460489)). "reviewer rR-N", "engineer rR-N" and "Codex rR-N" are rounds 2 to 5, and "reviewer r6b-N" the scoped check on revision 6b; #467's index links each one.
- A bare `§N` is a section of the draft ([part 1](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5932281730): §0–§3.2, including §3.1's shared items and §3.2's brief, which every card carries; [part 6](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5932283459): §4–§10). "The role answer" is in [part 3](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/467#issuecomment-5932282385). `m4-carry.md` is the coordinator's carry-over note, quoted in the draft's §0 and §8.

Card references are written as issue numbers, with the draft id beside each.

---

- **Labels:** `type:change`, `area:demo`.
- **Judges:** `reviewer` (O85), then `owner`. Its maker never merges it; the owner merges it, and that merge
  ratifies its README line (O14, `D21`). This replaces the hand edit revision 2 placed on the owner,
  as #466 replaced M3's (reviewer 14).
- **Depends on:** #490 (M4-10) merged.
- **Wave:** 10.
- **Claims:** none.
- **Lands in:** `docs/demo.gif`, `README.md:60`, and only those lines of `docs/demo.tape` the re-record
  needs, as item 2 bounds them.
- **Self-hosting paths:** none.

**Why.** #486 (M4-09a) changed the line the tape's `once` prints, the CI grep and the demo test. This card
re-records the GIF from the tape, and makes the alt text describe it. Revised on 2026-10-04 after the architect's [pre-dispatch review](https://github.com/williacj/rigger/issues/492#issuecomment-5984848827), F1–F5.

## Acceptance

1. `git diff` against the base changes no file but `docs/demo.gif`, the one line `README.md:60`, lines of `docs/demo.tape` under item 2, and one journal entry.
2. Where `docs/demo.tape` changes, the pull request names each changed line and the reason the re-record needs it. It also says whether the change alters what CI's demo job greps for. Where it does, the pull request shows the job's grep still matching at the head.
3. The committed `docs/demo.gif` is byte-identical to the `demo` artifact CI's demo job uploaded for the head commit, or for a run the pull request links. The pull request names the run, and the `vhs` version that job used.
4. The file the tape writes as the recording's final screen (`docs/demo.txt`, which is not tracked, per reviewer 23) holds the `once` line the CI demo job greps for. The pull request shows that screen in full.
5. CI's demo job passes at the head.
6. Every claim `README.md:60`'s alt text makes is shown on that final screen. The pull request quotes, for each claim, the line of the screen that shows it.
7. The alt text describes `once` claiming a card and dispatching its maker in the card's workspace, as the final screen names that workspace. It does not say the workspace was provisioned, since `once` prints nothing for provisioning (the demo's one step is `run: 'true'`, `test/demo-world.mjs:53`). Revised on 2026-10-05 under `R-LOOP-6`: item 6 governs, and this item gave way to it.
8. The alt text describes the outcome the screen shows: the stand-in maker exiting 0 with no pull request opened, and `once` exiting non-zero. It implies no finished card.
9. `git diff` against the base shows no other line of `README.md` changed.
10. `npm run lint:spec-style` reports no finding the change introduces, and the pull request gives the finding count at the base and at the head.
11. The pull request body says its README line is a proposal the owner ratifies by merging, and cites O14.
12. (shared) `npm test` exits 0 in a fresh clone of the head, run with `TMPDIR` set to a directory outside every checkout. The pull request gives that `TMPDIR`, the host's logical CPU count, and its one-minute load average read just before the run and just after it ends (O46: each figure "names its load at start and end"). The start load is no higher than twice the host's logical CPU count. Where O86 applies, the head's macOS CI runs stand in for this run.
13. (shared) Every test that failed on any run the maker made during the card is named in the pull request with its full failure output, as captured at the time. Where this change caused it, the head no longer fails it. Otherwise the pull request links a root-cause card filed for it, except in two cases, which take no card. A host stall is a run cancelled or timed out at ten or more times its bound while the host was not scheduling tests, as the run's durations show. The pull request names it with its output and says it takes no card. A run in a Linux cloud container is labelled history, and takes no card unless the failure recurs on macOS.
